description: Additional physical-dynamics base scenarios used to reduce repetition in canonical-concept-balanced runs.
notes: This file is a scenario source, not a standalone generation target.
It adds alternative base situations for concepts that previously had only one scenario in the core-plus-landmark pool.
The first expansion focuses on sink, spill, drain, leak, overflow, and guided downward flow.
The second expansion adds lift-up, absorb, compress, stretch, crack, dent, scatter, and stick scenarios.
The third expansion adds general roll/slide surface-friction and rotation-state cues without copying narrow benchmark wording.
The fourth expansion adds speed quantity-change cues: distance or marks per same time increase or decrease.
The fifth expansion adds speed endpoint-tendency cues: increasing speed creates collision or overshoot risk, while decreasing speed leads toward rest or stopping.

scenarios.cause_evidence: the slick table let the flat puck glide
scenarios.outcome_evidence: the puck moved forward with the same face upward

scenarios.material_or_surface: wood block on a wet tray
scenarios.rotation_evidence: the block kept its bottom face on the tray
scenarios.cause_evidence: the wet tray made the block's flat base easy to move
scenarios.outcome_evidence: the block moved sideways with its bottom face down

scenarios.rotation_allowed: surface did not catch the marble
scenarios.rotation_evidence: the marble glided with little turning
scenarios.cause_evidence: oil made the glass contact very slick
scenarios.outcome_evidence: the marble slid forward with little turning

scenarios.rotation_evidence: the boot kept the sole facing down
scenarios.cause_evidence: the icy step was slick under the boot
scenarios.outcome_evidence: the boot slid sideways while the sole stayed down

families.label: sink and float surface cue expansion
families.schema: Short surface, underwater, visibility, waterline, depth, and bottom-contact cues make sink/float evidence explicit without reusing benchmark objects.

scenarios.direction_evidence: the bead passed below the marked waterline
scenarios.cause_evidence: the glass bead was denser than the water
scenarios.outcome_evidence: the bead went below the waterline and ended underwater, fully covered

scenarios.direction_evidence: the chip disappeared underwater below the water surface
scenarios.cause_evidence: the ceramic chip was heavy for its size
scenarios.outcome_evidence: the chip went underwater and disappeared from view

scenarios.direction_evidence: the nut moved underwater from the surface area to the jar bottom
scenarios.cause_evidence: the brass nut was dense metal
scenarios.outcome_evidence: the nut reached the bottom underwater and no longer stayed near the surface

scenarios.direction_evidence: the cube moved deeper underwater through the water
scenarios.cause_evidence: the clay cube was solid and heavy
scenarios.outcome_evidence: the cube lost height and moved deeper underwater in the tank

scenarios.direction_evidence: the disk stayed visible at the water surface
scenarios.cause_evidence: the cork disk was light and buoyant
scenarios.outcome_evidence: the disk stayed on the surface and remained visible

scenarios.direction_evidence: the plug rose until part of it was above the water
scenarios.cause_evidence: air in the foam supported the plug
scenarios.outcome_evidence: the plug stayed partly above the water surface

scenarios.geometry_or_medium: tank with a blue water mark
scenarios.direction_evidence: the lid stayed above the marked waterline
scenarios.cause_evidence: sealed air inside the lid made it buoyant
scenarios.outcome_evidence: the lid stayed above the waterline and did not go under

scenarios.direction_evidence: the button kept the same level at the surface
scenarios.cause_evidence: the wax button was less dense than the water
scenarios.outcome_evidence: the button stayed at the same surface level
